questions.question: In an election there were only two candidates. 20% of the voters did not cast their votes and 1000 votes were declared invalid. The winner, by obtaining 70% of the total valid votes, defeated his rival by 1200 votes. The total number of voters in the election was ________.
questions.questionHtml: In an election there were only two candidates. 20% of the voters did not cast their votes and 1000 votes were declared invalid. The winner, by obtaining 70% of the total valid votes, defeated his rival by 1200 votes. The total number of voters in the election was ________.
questions.solution:
Given:

Percentage of voters did not cast their votes = 20%

Invalid votes = 1000

Winner votes = 70% of valid votes

Winner candidate defeated his rival by = 1200 votes

Calculation:

According to question, 

30% of the total valid votes = 1200

⇒ 0.3 × Total valid votes = 1200

⇒ Total valid votes = 1200/0.3 = 4000

Now, Total voters = 4000 + 1000 = 5000

Hence, the Total voters are 5000.

Alternate MethodLet the total valid votes be 100 

Now winning candidate received 70% votes, 

hence losing candidate will get 30% votes, 

The difference between them is, 

⇒ 70% - 30% = 40%

Now as per the question, 

⇒ 40% = 1200

⇒ 1% = 30

Hence, total valid votes, 

⇒ 100% = 100 × 30 = 3000

Invalid votes = 1000

Now, total casted votes = 3000 + 1000 = 4000

20% did not cast their votes, 

Hence, 80% = 4000

⇒ 1% = 4000/80 = 50

⇒ 100% = 50 × 100 = 5000

∴ The number of voters is 5000.

questions.question: A sells 2 TV sets at equal price, one at a loss of 15% and another at a profit of 15%. Find the loss/gain percentage in the overall transaction?
questions.questionHtml: A sells 2 TV sets at equal price, one at a loss of 15% and another at a profit of 15%. Find the loss/gain percentage in the overall transaction?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

L oss percentage = 152/100 = 225/100 = 2.25%

Given:

A sells 2 TV sets, one at a loss of 15% and another at profit of 15%.

Concept:

When two articles are sold at same price but one of them at sold at x% profit and another sold at x% loss, in this process there is always loss = x2/100

Calculation:

15% = 3/20

Let selling price of each article be Rs. 391 (LCM of 23 and 17)

Total selling price of both articles = 391 × 2 = 782

⇒ Cost price of first article = 391 × 20/17 = 460

⇒ Cost price of second article = 391 × 20/23 = 340

⇒ Total cost price of both articles = 460 + 340 = 800

⇒ Loss = 800 – 782 = Rs. 18

∴ Loss% = 18/800 × 100 = 2.25%

questions.question: A batsman scored 124 runs, which included 6 boundaries and 10 sixes. What percentage of his total score did he make by running between the wickets?
questions.questionHtml: A batsman scored 124 runs, which included 6 boundaries and 10 sixes. What percentage of his total score did he make by running between the wickets?
questions.solution:
Given:

Total score of the batsman = 124 run

He has hitten 6 boundaries and 10 sixes

Calculation:

The batsman scored from boundaries = 6 × 4

⇒ 24 runs

The batsman scored from sixes = 10 × 6

⇒ 60 runs

Total runs scored by running between the wickets = 124 - (24 + 60)

⇒ 124 - 84

⇒ 40 runs

Required % = (40/124) × 100

⇒ \(32\frac{8}{31}\)

∴ He scored \(32\frac{8}{31}\%\) of his total score by running between the wickets.

questions.question: What is the % profit on the cost price of an article if there is a profit of 20% on the selling price?
questions.questionHtml: What is the % profit on the cost price of an article if there is a profit of 20% on the selling price?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Profit on Selling Price = 20% = 1/5

This means SP = 5 units, Profit = 1 unit.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Profit = 5 − 1 = 4 units.

Actual Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 4) × 100 = 25%.

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Profit calculated on Selling Price (SP) = 20%

Formula Used:

CP = SP − Profit

Actual Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let Selling Price (SP) = 100 units

⇒ Profit = 20% of 100 = 20 units

⇒ Cost Price (CP) = 100 − 20 = 80 units

⇒ Actual Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Actual Profit % = (20 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Actual Profit % = 1/4 × 100 = 25%

∴ The correct answer is 25%.

Additional Information

Loss Calculated on Selling Price

If a loss is given as x% on SP, then CP = SP + Loss. The actual loss percentage is (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) unless stated otherwise. Selling Price = MP − (Discount % of MP).

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = (Error ÷ (True Value − Error)) × 100.

questions.question: In a triangle ABC, AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC and ∠BAD = 60°. What is the length of AD?
questions.questionHtml: In a triangle ABC, AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC and ∠BAD = 60°. What is the length of AD?
questions.solution:
Given :

AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC

∠BAD = 60° 

Formula used :

Area of a triangle when θ has given = 1/2 × Adjacent sides × sinθ    

Calculations:

Let AD = h,

Using the formula discussed above,

⇒ \(Area \space of\space \triangle ABC = \frac {1}{2} \times b\times c\times sin\angle BAC\)

⇒ \(\frac {1}{2}\times b\times c\times sin 120\)       ----(1)

We know that, 

sin(90∘ + 30∘) = cos 30∘ = √3/2

Hence from equation (1)

⇒ Area of Δ ABC =  \(\frac{√3}{4}bc\)

Similarly, 

⇒ \(Area \space of \space \triangle BAD = \frac{√ 3}{4}ch\)

⇒ \(Area \space of \space \triangle CAD = \frac{√ 3}{4}bh\)

Area of Δ ABC = Area of Δ BAD + Area of Δ CAD

⇒ \(\frac{√ 3}{4}bc = \frac{√ 3}{4}ch + \frac{√ 3}{4}bh\)

⇒ bc = h (b + c)

∴ The length of AD = \( \frac{bc}{b+c}\)

questions.question: Susanth purchased 3 packs of oil at the rate of Rs. 20 each, 4 packs of oil at Rs. 21 each and 3 packs of oil at the rate of Rs. 22 each. What is the average cost of one pack of oil?
questions.questionHtml: Susanth purchased 3 packs of oil at the rate of Rs. 20 each, 4 packs of oil at Rs. 21 each and 3 packs of oil at the rate of Rs. 22 each. What is the average cost of one pack of oil?
questions.solution:
Given:

3 packs of oil at Rs. 20 each.

4 packs of oil at Rs. 21 each.

3 packs of oil at Rs. 22 each.

Formula Used:

Average cost = Total cost of oil packs / Total number of oil packs

Calculation:

Total cost for 3 packs at Rs. 20 = 3 × 20 = Rs. 60

Total cost for 4 packs at Rs. 21 = 4 × 21 = Rs. 84

Total cost for 3 packs at Rs. 22 = 3 × 22 = Rs. 66

Total cost for all packs = 60 + 84 + 66 = Rs. 210

Total number of packs = 3 + 4 + 3 = 10

Average cost = 210 / 10

Average cost = Rs. 21

The average cost of one pack of oil is Rs. 21.

questions.question: The six-digit number N = 4a6b9c is divisible by 99, then the maximum sum of the digits of N is:
questions.questionHtml: The six-digit number N = 4a6b9c is divisible by 99, then the maximum sum of the digits of N is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Number N = 4a6b9c must be divisible by 9 and 11.

Sum of digits (4 + a + 6 + b + 9 + c) = 19 + a + b + c must be a multiple of 9.

Maximum possible sum of digits for any six-digit number is 54, but here it is 19 + a + b + c.

Since a, b, c ≤ 9, max (19 + a + b + c) = 19 + 27 = 46. Possible sums divisible by 9 are 27, 36, 45.

For divisibility by 11: (c + b + a) − (9 + 6 + 4) = (a + b + c) − 19 must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

If (a + b + c) − 19 = 0 ⇒ a + b + c = 19. Total sum = 19 + 19 = 38 (not divisible by 9). If (a + b + c) − 19 = 11 ⇒ a + b + c = 30. Total sum = 19 + 30 = 49 (not divisible by 9). If (a + b + c) − 19 = −11 ⇒ a + b + c = 8. Total sum = 19 + 8 = 27.

∴ The correct answer is 27.

Alternate Method

Given: Number N = 4a6b9c is divisible by 99.

Formula: For divisibility by 99, the number must be divisible by 9 and 11.

⇒ Divisibility by 9: 4 + a + 6 + b + 9 + c = 19 + a + b + c must be divisible by 9.

⇒ Divisibility by 11: Sum of digits at odd places − Sum of digits at even places = (c + b + a) − (9 + 6 + 4) = (a + b + c) − 19.

⇒ For divisibility by 11, (a + b + c) − 19 must be 0, 11, 22... or −11, −22...

⇒ Case 1: a + b + c − 19 = 0 ⇒ a + b + c = 19. Sum of digits = 19 + 19 = 38 (Not divisible by 9).

⇒ Case 2: a + b + c − 19 = 11 ⇒ a + b + c = 30. Sum of digits = 19 + 30 = 49 (Not divisible by 9).

⇒ Case 3: a + b + c − 19 = −11 ⇒ a + b + c = 8. Sum of digits = 19 + 8 = 27 (Divisible by 9).

⇒ Maximum possible value for (a + b + c) is 27. Checking if sum of digits can be 36 or 45: if sum = 36, a+b+c = 17. 17−19 = −2 (not div by 11). If sum = 45, a+b+c = 26. 26−19 = 7 (not div by 11).

∴ The correct answer is 27.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Composite Divisibility

If a number is divisible by two co-prime numbers a and b, then it is also divisible by their product (a × b).

questions.question: In a class of 5 students, the average weight of the 4 lightest students is 40 kgs, Average weight of the 4 heaviest students is 45 kgs. What is the difference between the maximum and minimum possible average weight overall?
questions.questionHtml: In a class of 5 students, the average weight of the 4 lightest students is 40 kgs, Average weight of the 4 heaviest students is 45 kgs. What is the difference between the maximum and minimum possible average weight overall?
questions.solution:
Given:- 

(1) Total students = 5

(2)The average weight of the 4 lightest students is 40 kg

(3) Average weight of the 4 heaviest students is 45
 
Formula used:- 

Average = Sum of all values ÷ Total number of values 

Calculation:-

Let the 5 students in ascending order of their weight be a, b, c, d, e

Condition(1)

The average weight of the 4 lightest students is 40 kg 

⇒ Average = (a + b + c + d)/4 = 40   

⇒ (a + b + c + d) =160......(1) 

Condition(2) 

The average weight of the 4 heaviest students is 45 kg

⇒ (b + c + d + e)/4 = 45   

⇒ (b + c + d + e) = 180....(2)

Subtract from equations (1) and (2) 

⇒ e = 20 + a … (3)  

For the least possible average, we need the least value of a and e
  
The least value of e can be 45 and ( b = c = d = 45 ).

The least value of a can be ⇒ 20 + a = 45 

⇒ a = 25 

Now the least average = (25 + 45 + 45 + 45 +45)/5 = 41 .....(4)

For the maximum possible average,

We need the maximum possible value of a and e   

The maximum value of a can be 40 and ( b = c = d = 40 ).

The maximum value of e can be = 40 + 20 = 60 

For the maximum possible average

= (60 + 40 + 40 + 40 + 40)/5 = 44 .....(5) 

Now difference 44 − 41 = 3     
 
 ∴ The required answer is 3.0

Study the given table and answer the question that follows.

The table shows the population of three cities P, Q and R, as percentage of the total population of these three cities taken together.  CITY  POPULATION  ABOVE   60  M ∶ F (BELOW 60   YEARS)
 P  45%  30%  3 ∶ 7
 Q  30%  70%  3 ∶ 1

Find the male population of city R that is below 60 years.
questions.solution:
Given:

 CITY  POPULATION  ABOVE   60  M ∶ F (BELOW 60   YEARS)
 P  45%  30%  3 ∶ 7
 Q  30%  70%  3 ∶ 1

Concept Used:

Basic Percentage Calculation

Calculation:

Population of city R = \(\frac{25}{100}\times 300000=75000\)

Population above 60 years = \(\frac{40}{100}\times 75000=30000\)

Hence, the male population in the city R for the age below 60 years is 21,600.

questions.question: The area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm is
questions.questionHtml: The area of a triangle whose sides are 13 cm, 14 cm and 15 cm is
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Calculate semi-perimeter (s): s = (13 + 14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 42 ÷ 2 = 21 cm.

Apply Heron's Formula directly: Area = √[21 × (21−13) × (21−14) × (21−15)].

Area = √[21 × 8 × 7 × 6] = √[7056] = 84 cm2.

∴ The correct answer is 84 cm2.

Alternate Method

Given: Sides of the triangle are a = 13 cm, b = 14 cm, and c = 15 cm.

Formula Used: Heron's Formula for the area of a triangle = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s is the semi-perimeter.

⇒ Semi-perimeter (s) = (a + b + c) ÷ 2

⇒ s = (13 + 14 + 15) ÷ 2

⇒ s = 42 ÷ 2 = 21 cm

⇒ Area = √[21 × (21 − 13) × (21 − 14) × (21 − 15)]

⇒ Area = √[21 × 8 × 7 × 6]

⇒ Area = √[3 × 7 × 2 × 4 × 7 × 2 × 3]

⇒ Area = √[(3 × 3) × (7 × 7) × (2 × 2) × 4]

⇒ Area = 3 × 7 × 2 × 2

⇒ Area = 84 cm2

∴ The correct answer is 84 cm2.

Additional Information

Heron's Formula

Used to find the area of a scalene triangle when all three sides are known: Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)].

Right-Angled Triangle Area

If the base and height are known, the area is calculated using 1/2 × base × height.

Equilateral Triangle Area

For a triangle with all sides equal to 'a', the area is (√3 ÷ 4) × a2.

Semi-perimeter (s)

It is half of the perimeter of the triangle, calculated as s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.

one of the roots of quadratic equation 7x2 - 50x + k = 0 is 7

Calculation:

According to the question

On putting x = 7 in 7x2 - 50x + k = 0, we get

⇒ 7(7)2 - 50 × 7 + k = 0

⇒ 343 - 350 + k = 0

⇒ k = 350 - 343

⇒ k = 7

∴ The required value of k is 7.

questions.question: If tanθ = \(\frac{8}{19}\) , find the value of sec 2 θ.
questions.questionHtml: If tanθ = \(\frac{8}{19}\), find the value of sec2θ.
questions.solution:
sec2θ = tan2θ + 1

sec2θ = (8/19)2 + 1

⇒  1 + (64/361)  = \(1\frac{64}{361}\)

questions.question: In the diagram, ABCD is a rectangle with XY on BC such that BX : XY : YC = 7 : 5 : 8. Find the ratio of the area of triangle DXY to the area of quadrilateral ABXD
questions.questionHtml: In the diagram, ABCD is a rectangle with XY on BC such that  BX : XY : YC = 7 : 5 : 8. Find the ratio of the area of triangle DXY to the area of quadrilateral ABXD
questions.solution:
Calculation:

Let the common ratio for the rectangle be "a"

⇒ BX = 7a

⇒ XY = 5a

⇒ YC = 8a

Area of Δ DYC = \(1\over2\) × 8a × DC = 4a × DC

Similarly, Δ XDC = \(1\over2\) × (8a + 5a) × DC = \(13a\over2\) × DC

Area of Δ DXY = \(13a \over 2\)× DC - 4a × DC = \(5a\over2\) × DC

Area of ABCD = (7a + 5a + 8a) × DC = 20a × DC

Area of quadrilateral ABXD = Area of ABCD - Area of Δ XDC

⇒ 20a × DC -  \(13a\over2\) × DC =  \(27a\over2\) × DC

The ratio of the area Δ DXY : Area of quadrilateral ABXD 

⇒  \({{5a\over2}{\times DC}}\over{27a\over2}\times DC\) = 5 : 27

The required ratio of the area is 5 : 27

questions.question: A vertical pole and a vertical tower are on the same level of ground in such a way that from the top of the pole, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is 60º and the angle of depression of the bottom of the tower is 30º. If the height of the tower is 76 m, then find the height (in m) of the pole.

questions.solution:
In ΔACD, tan 30° = CD/AD

⇒ 1/√3 = x/AD ⇒ AD = √3x   .....(1)

In ΔAED, tan 60° = ED/AD

⇒ √3 = (76 - x)/√3x ⇒ 76 - x = 3x ⇒ 3x + x = 76 ⇒ x = 76/4 = 19

questions.question: A, B and C working separately can do a piece of work in 11 days, 20 days and 55 days, respectively. If they work together, then the time taken to complete the work is:
questions.questionHtml: A, B and C working separately can do a piece of work in 11 days, 20 days and 55 days, respectively. If they work together, then the time taken to complete the work is:
questions.solution:
Given:

A can complete the work in 11 days

B can complete the work in 20 days

C can complete the work in 55 days

Formula used:

Work done per day = \(\frac{1}{\text{Time taken}}\)

Total work done per day by A, B, and C = \(\frac{1}{11} + \frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{55}\)

Time taken when working together = \(\frac{1}{\text{Total work per day}}\)

Calculation:

Total work per day = \(\frac{1}{11} + \frac{1}{20} + \frac{1}{55}\)

LCM of 11, 20, and 55 = 220

Total work per day = \(\frac{20}{220} + \frac{11}{220} + \frac{4}{220} = \frac{35}{220}\)

Total work per day = \(\frac{7}{44}\)

Time taken when working together = \(\frac{1}{\frac{7}{44}} = \frac{44}{7}\) = \(6\frac{2}{7}\) days

∴ The time taken to complete the work is approximately \(6\frac{2}{7}\) days.
